newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire talks postponed until Saturday.
newsitem.headline: Zaire talks postponed until Saturday.

text.p: Talks between President Mobutu Sese Seko and Zaire rebel leader Laurent Kabila have been put off until Saturday because the harbour in Libreville, Gabon, cannot accommodate the ship they plan to meet on, Mobutu's son said on Thursday.
The meeting, initially planned for Friday off Gabon, will take place on a South African navy ship in international waters in the Atlantic off the coast of Central Africa.
"The meeting is postponed till Saturday because the ship cannot get into harbour at Libreville. The harbour is too short," Nzanga Mobutu told Reuters by telephone.
He said Mobutu and his team would travel to neighbouring Congo on Friday and the meeting would be launched from the Congolese port of Pointe Noire.
Mobutu, debilitated by cancer, agreed on Wednesday to meet Kabila face to face on the ship off Gabon after lengthy meetings with U.S. troubleshooter Bill Richardson.

Sources close to the negotiations said Mobutu, whose clan is anxious to retain a stake in the future of their mineral-rich nation, had declined a plan for him to fly to the ship by helicopter. The sources said he agreed to seaborne talks after being told he could board in Libreville.
Mobutu had planned to leave for Libreville on Thursday.

"The president is not leaving and the journey is cancelled for today. This is not Zaire's decision and there's no health reason but we understand the talks have been postponed until Saturday," Information Minister Kin-Kiey Mulumba said earlier.
Kabila, whose rebels took up arms in October and control over half of Zaire, is insisting that Mobutu stand down. His forces are marching on the capital Kinshasa.
